items.title: Disruption of the TCF7L1-TLE3 Complex by Sulforaphane De-Represses TFRC Transcription to Overcome Chemoresistance Through Ferroptosis in Pancreatic Cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is among the most lethal malignancies. Inducing ferroptosis is a promising strategy to enhance chemotherapy and overcome resistance in PDAC. However, the transcriptional control of transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC, encoding the TFR1 protein), the iron gateway driving ferroptosis remains unknown in PDAC, hindering the development of TFR1-targeted ferroptosis-inducing strategies. In this study, TCF7L1 is identified as the first transcriptional repressor of TFRC in PDAC, defining a new ferroptosis iron regulator. TCF7L1 knockdown induces ferroptosis and suppresses tumor growth in patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and xenograft (PDX) models, but not in normal human cell lines, revealing its cancer-selective ferroptosis dependency. Sulforaphane (SFN) binds to TCF7L1 through a binding interface that involves Tyr148, Lys165, and His186, inducing a conformational change that disrupts the TCF7L1-TLE3 corepressor interaction. This disruption relieves TCF7L1-mediated transcriptional repression of TFRC, leading to Fe2+ overload, thereby triggering ferroptosis. Combined treatment with SFN and the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3 nearly abolishes PDAC growth. The TCF7L1-TFR1 axis determines chemosensitivity and acquired resistance. SFN enhances gemcitabine sensitivity and overcomes drug resistance. This study concludes that the TCF7L1-TFR1 axis is a druggable target and SFN is the first direct TCF7L1 ligand, providing a safe, translatable strategy to sensitize PDAC.

items.title: Photodynamic therapy induces apoptosis and downregulates immune checkpoint transcripts in pancreatic cancer cells.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a five-year survival rate below 10%. Most cases are unresectable, and treatment is hampered by dense stroma, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a minimally invasive modality that kills tumor cells via reactive oxygen species and may modulate immunoregulatory molecules. The effect of zinc phthalocyanine (ZnPc)-mediated PDT on immune checkpoint expression in PDAC has not been characterized.
METHODS: Immune checkpoint gene expression was compared between pancreatic tumor and normal tissue using TCGA-PAAD and GTEx datasets via GEPIA2. MIA PaCa-2 and PANC-1 cell lines were treated with ZnPc-PDT (675 nm; 80 mW; 12 J/cm2). Cytotoxicity was measured by MTT assay, apoptosis and cell-cycle distribution were analyzed by flow cytometry, and transcript levels of CD47, CTLA-4, PD-L1, and VISTA, together with the apoptosis-related genes BAX and BCL2, were quantified by RT-qPCR and normalized to GAPDH.
RESULTS: In silico analysis showed significantly higher expression of CD47, CTLA-4, and VISTA in PDAC than in normal pancreas, whereas the difference for PD-L1 was not significant. ZnPc alone showed no cytotoxicity; light activation produced dose-dependent cell death with IC50 values of 0.784 μg/mL (MIA PaCa-2) and 0.09 μg/mL (PANC-1). Flow cytometric analysis showed that ZnPc-PDT significantly increased the percentage of apoptotic cells in both cell lines. Cell-cycle analysis revealed an increase in the sub-G1 fraction in both cell lines. MIA PaCa-2 cells also showed a modest but significant increase in the G0/G1 fraction. ZnPc-PDT increased BAX and decreased BCL2 transcript levels in both cell lines. Treatment with ZnPc-PDT significantly downregulated CD47, CTLA-4, and PD-L1 transcript levels in both cell lines, whereas VISTA was downregulated only in PANC-1 cells.
CONCLUSIONS: ZnPc-PDT induced light-dependent cytotoxicity and consistently downregulated the transcript levels of CD47, CTLA-4, and PD-L1 in PDAC cells, while VISTA regulation is cell-line dependent. These in vitro findings warrant protein-level and immune-functional validation before combinations of PDT with immune checkpoint inhibitors are explored for PDAC.

items.title: ACTN4 promotes invasive phenotypes and WNT/β-catenin signaling through HDAC7-DACT2 regulation in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits invasive growth and resistance to gemcitabine. We investigated how the actin-binding protein ACTN4 connects invasive behavior with WNT/β-catenin signaling. Elevated ACTN4 expression was associated with poorer survival in public PDAC cohorts and metastatic disease in genetically engineered mice. ACTN4 depletion reduced TGF-β1-induced invasion, focal adhesion signaling, and WNT activity, while increasing gemcitabine sensitivity in cells and organoids. Biochemical analyses and genetic rescue experiments linked Ser159-dependent ACTN4 activity to HDAC7 stability, reduced DACT2 expression, and β-catenin-dependent transcription. DACT2 depletion partially reversed the effects of ACTN4 loss. Ellagic acid reduced ACTN4-HDAC7 complex recovery and attenuated associated signaling. These findings support a functional model connecting ACTN4 to HDAC7-DACT2 regulation and identify an ACTN4-associated signaling axis relevant to PDAC invasion and gemcitabine response.

items.title: Drug-tolerant persister states in pancreatic cancer and their therapeutic vulnerabilities.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) rapidly develops therapeutic resistance, leading to frequent relapse even after an initial response to treatment. Drug-tolerant persister cells represent a transient and plastic population that survives cytotoxic pressure through reversible adaptive programs and may subsequently give rise to stable resistant disease. In PDAC, persister survival is supported by metabolic rewiring, redox adaptation, post-translational remodeling, autophagy, and lysosomal fitness, together with protective signals provided by the desmoplastic tumor microenvironment. These mechanisms preserve cellular homeostasis, sustain mitochondrial function, modify drug handling, and reduce immune recognition under conditions of severe therapeutic and metabolic stress. Experimental systems based on treatment-pulse protocols, patient-derived organoids, stromal co-cultures, relapse models, and single-cell approaches are beginning to define the functional dependencies of these residual populations. This review discusses the biological boundaries of PDAC persister states and examines their principal therapeutic vulnerabilities. Understanding when these adaptive programs emerge may enable the development of time-resolved strategies aimed at eliminating residual tumor cells before reversible tolerance progresses to stable resistance and clinical relapse.

items.title: TIPARP promotes M2-like macrophage polarization and associates with T2D myeloid alterations and PDAC progression.
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is associated with increased pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) risk, and diabetes-associated myeloid alterations may contribute to this relationship. We integrated single-cell analyses, Mendelian randomization (MR), and cellular and mouse models to investigate TIPARP-associated myeloid states. TIPARP expression was enriched in T2D classical monocytes, with predicted interactions involving macrophage-like monocytes. MR suggested a nominal association between genetically predicted higher TIPARP expression and PDAC risk (odds ratio [OR] = 2.15, p = 0.0044), with colocalization evidence (posterior probability of hypothesis 4 [PPH4] = 0.8023). TIPARP overexpression promoted M2-like polarization in THP-1-derived and primary human macrophages with PI3K-AKT involvement. Conditioned media from TIPARP-overexpressing macrophages enhanced PDAC cell proliferation and migration, while macrophage co-injection was associated with larger xenograft tumors. Matched blood and tumor samples showed associations between circulating TIPARP-positive (TIPARP+) classical monocytes, intratumoral TIPARP+ macrophages, and M2-like signatures. These findings suggest that TIPARP-associated myeloid alterations may represent a potential immunological link between T2D and PDAC progression.

items.title: High-risk pancreatic cancer pathology reveals a B3GNT3-associated glycosylation program.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pancreatic cancer has a poor prognosis and marked heterogeneity, whereas existing pathomics models generally lack biological interpretability. We aimed to construct the pathomics prognostic score GlyPath-Risk and explore the molecular states associated with the high-risk phenotype captured by the score.
METHODS: We integrated H&E whole-slide images from TCGA-PAAD and Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (FMUUH), extracted handcrafted and deep-learning features using CellProfiler and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, and constructed GlyPath-Risk using a combined LASSO and random survival forest model. Prognostic performance was evaluated in training, internal validation, and FMUUH cohorts. Correlation analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and xCell immune-infiltration estimation were used to investigate associations among GlyPath-Risk, the glycosylation transcriptional program, and the tumor microenvironment. Single-cell transcriptomics, CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, Geneformer virtual perturbation, and B3GNT3 knockdown experiments were used to generate and evaluate candidate biological hypotheses.
RESULTS: GlyPath-Risk comprised six pathological features and showed C-indices of 0.88, 0.68, and 0.83 in the training, internal validation, and FMUUH cohorts, respectively. Its association with overall survival remained after adjustment for age, sex, and clinical stage in the reported Cox model (multivariable HR = 1.230). The glycosylation gene set showed the strongest mean absolute correlation with pathological features among 20 post-translational modification classes. WGCNA identified six co-expression modules significantly associated with GlyPath-Risk (BH-FDR < 0.05), including a blue module containing B3GNT3. Immune-cell score analyses showed nominal associations with selected immune- and vascular-related scores, but none of 51 candidate scores reached BH-FDR < 0.05. Single-cell analysis suggested differences in predicted outgoing communication from B3GNT3-high and B3GNT3-low tumor cells, while virtual perturbation identified transcriptional states associated with perturbation sensitivity. B3GNT3 knockdown was associated with reduced proliferation and altered macrophage-associated markers in conditioned-medium experiments.
CONCLUSION: GlyPath-Risk showed prognostic associations across the evaluated cohorts. The score was associated with a B3GNT3-related glycosylation transcriptional program and may be related to immune- and vascular-related transcriptomic features. These findings provide a testable framework for investigating the biological correlates of pathomics scores and nominate B3GNT3 as a candidate molecular anchor requiring independent validation.

items.title: Matrix cues modulate neurotrophic signaling through PIEZO1 in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is highly aggressive and has a poor prognosis. Perineural invasion (PNI), a characteristic pathological feature of PDAC, is closely associated with postoperative recurrence and cancer-related pain. PDAC is also characterized by a prominent fibrotic microenvironment, but how tumor cells sense abnormal matrix cues and translate them into signals related to neural invasion remains unclear. In this study, we established distinct matrix conditions using different GelMA concentrations and combined transcriptomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses, cellular functional assays, and tissue validation to examine the potential role of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 in matrix responses and neurotrophic alterations in PDAC. Different GelMA conditions altered PDAC cell aggregation and intracellular Ca2+ levels and were accompanied by extensive transcriptional remodeling. Mechanosensing-related genes, including PIEZO1, and genes associated with neurotrophic signaling, including BDNF, changed across matrix conditions. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed that PIEZO1 was enriched in PDAC PNI regions and displayed a spatial gradient: F2RL1/PAR2 was also enriched in PNI regions. Public database analysis showed that high F2RL1 expression was associated with shorter survival and positively correlated with PIEZO1 expression. Pharmacological modulation of PIEZO1 activity was accompanied by corresponding changes in NGF, BDNF, PRSS1, and F-actin. In mouse PNI tissues, PIEZO1 inhibition reduced PIEZO1, NGF, and PRSS1 expression and attenuated the EMT-related phenotype. These findings connect GelMA-dependent cellular responses with PIEZO1-associated signaling and identify PRSS1 and PAR2 as candidate molecules involved in PDAC PNI.

items.title: Comparing health outcomes and costs of care by discharge disposition after hepatopancreatic cancer surgery: Insights from SEER-medicare.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated post-acute care settings, clinical outcomes, and Medicare costs after hepatopancreatic cancer surgery in older adults with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) or intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA).
METHODS: Using SEER-Medicare (2005-2019), patients ≥65 years who had stage I-III resection were categorized by discharge disposition: home, home health agency (HHA), skilled nursing facility (SNF), or interhospital transfer. Multivariable regression assessed associations with outcomes, expenditures, and factors linked to non-home discharge.
RESULTS: Among 4646 patients (median age 74), 46.7% went home, 32.6% to HHA, 17.2% to SNF, and 3.4% transferred. Minority patients and those undergoing urgent surgery were more often discharged to HHA or SNF. Compared with HHA, SNF discharge was associated with lower odds of receiving adjuvant chemotherapy (aOR 0.54) and oncology follow-up (aOR 0.65), higher 90-day mortality (aOR 2.06) and readmission (aOR 1.32). Interhospital transfer also increased 90-day mortality (aOR 2.38). Home discharge reduced 90-day readmission odds (aOR 0.78)0.4646 patients, 46.7% were discharged home, 32.6% to HHA, 17.2% to SNF, and 3.4% to transfer. Median age was 74 years (IQR 70-80).
CONCLUSION: SNF discharge after high-risk HP cancer surgery is linked to worse outcomes and higher costs; HHA and home discharge show better recovery and value.

items.title: Alternative splicing as a multilayered regulatory hub in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Alternative splicing is a crucial regulator of transcriptomic plasticity in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and its dysregulation contributes to tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and disease heterogeneity. While mutations in spliceosomal components or splice-site sequences can directly affect splicing, evidence increasingly suggests that aberrant splicing in PDAC results more often from the coordinated disruption of multiple regulatory layers. These layers include chromatin organization, transcriptional dynamics, epigenetic and epitranscriptomic mechanisms, and RNA-binding protein networks. Together, these interconnected processes reshape the transcript isoform landscape, producing oncogenic variants that facilitate tumor progression, metabolic adaptation, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. This review synthesizes the current knowledge on the multilayered regulation of alternative splicing in PDAC, distinguishing mechanisms that directly determine splice-site selection from those that act indirectly by regulating splicing factors, and from RNA regulatory layers that interact with, but can operate independently of, alternative splicing. Focusing on the dynamic interplay among co-transcriptional chromatin regulation, transcriptional kinetics, RNA modifications, and non-coding RNA-mediated regulatory networks, we examine how these mechanisms collectively remodel the splicing landscape to support tumor plasticity and malignant progression, while critically assessing the strength of PDAC-specific evidence and highlighting areas where mechanistic understanding remains incomplete. Additionally, we highlight emerging opportunities for isoform-level biomarker development and splicing-directed therapeutic strategies, while outlining the major challenges that must be addressed for their successful clinical translation.

items.title: Serum extracellular vesicle proteomics reveals treatment-associated biomarkers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Longitudinal biomarkers of treatment response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are needed. Extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched serum proteomics may provide a minimally invasive approach for monitoring systemic and tumor-associated responses to therapy.
METHODS: Paired pre-treatment and post-treatment serum samples were analyzed from 51 patients with pancreatic cancer, including 25 treated with FOLFIRINOX and 20 treated with gemcitabine-based therapy. EVs were enriched using the Mag-Net method and profiled by data independent acquisition mass spectrometry. After batch correction and filtering, 941 proteins were retained for differential and pathway analyses. Paired linear models and gene set enrichment analyses were used to assess treatment-associated changes. Baseline protein abundance and longitudinal changes were evaluated in relation to overall survival (OS) using Cox models.
RESULTS: A total of 2,089 EV-associated proteins were identified, with an average of 1,186 proteins quantified per sample. Across the cohort, 26 proteins differed between post- and pretreatment samples. Proteins that increased after treatment were primarily related to extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion, whereas proteins that decreased after treatment were associated with actin cytoskeletal organization, coagulation, and hemostasis. Treatment-associated changes were more pronounced in the FOLFIRINOX group, in which 32 proteins were differentially expressed. FOLFIRINOX was characterized by coordinated reductions in platelet- and coagulation-associated proteins, including PF4, PF4V1, PPBP, GP5, ITGA2B, and ITGB3, accompanied by enrichment of platelet activation, coagulation, and hemostasis pathways among down-regulated processes. No individual proteins met the same significance threshold in the gemcitabine group. A composite seven-protein platelet score decreased significantly after FOLFIRINOX but not for gemcitabine, and the between-regimen difference in score change was significant. Higher pretreatment ITGB1 abundance was associated with longer OS after multiple-testing correction (HR, 0.112; BH-FDR = 0.0063). In multivariable analysis, greater treatment-associated platelet-score depletion was independently associated with shorter OS (HR per unit increase in Δscore, 0.56; P = 0.030).
CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal serum EV-enriched proteomics identified treatment-associated biological changes in PDAC, including a coordinated platelet-related response predominantly observed after FOLFIRINOX. Baseline ITGB1 abundance and longitudinal platelet-score changes represent potentially complementary prognostic and pharmacodynamic markers. These findings are exploratory and require validation in larger, independent cohorts incorporating platelet counts, coagulation measurements, and targeted proteomic assays.

items.title: Complement C1q drives skeletal muscle wasting in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Cancer cachexia, defined by involuntary skeletal muscle loss, affects ~ 70% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients at diagnosis and independently worsens survival. Here, we identify complement component 1q (C1q) as a driver of PDAC-induced muscle wasting, with coordinated effects across muscle, tumor, and systemic inflammatory compartments. In cachectic PDAC patient muscle, C1q partially co-deposits with IgM, and C1q mRNA correlates with reduced muscle radiation attenuation, a CT-derived measure of muscle quality. In PDAC tumors, C1q protein correlates with immunosuppressive programs and independently predicts poor survival. These findings are recapitulated in orthotopic KPC mice, where C1q mRNA is upregulated in respiratory muscle before cachexia onset, and C1q deposits in tumors and co-deposits with IgM in muscles of cachectic mice. C1qa deletion reduced systemic inflammatory mediators, blocked muscle atrophy, and improved activity and grip strength in KPC mice, while attenuating immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix remodeling in respiratory muscle. Host C1qa deletion also suppressed angiogenic and immunosuppressive programs in KPC tumors, while increasing intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell density and Granzyme B production. These findings position C1q as a driver of cancer-induced muscle wasting and tumor immunosuppression, supporting C1q inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy targeting pathological features of poor-prognosis PDAC.

items.title: Differentiating early-stage pancreatic cancer from benign masses: the diagnostic superiority of immuno-nutritional indices.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The accurate preoperative differentiation of early-stage pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from benign/premalignant masses remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic value of systemic immuno-nutritional indices (CALLY, PNI, NLR, PLR, CAR) in predicting early-stage PDAC by excluding the statistical bias created by advanced-stage tumor burden.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 75 patients who underwent surgical resection for a pancreatic mass between September 2020 and February 2026. Patients were divided into an early-stage (Stage 1 and 2 A) malignant group (n = 21) and a benign/premalignant group (n = 54). The diagnostic performance of indices calculated from routine preoperative blood tests was evaluated using ROC curve and multivariate logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: In the malignant group, NLR (p = 0.010) and PLR (p = 0.007) were significantly higher, whereas PNI (p = 0.001) and CALLY (p = 0.011) indices were significantly lower compared to the benign group. ROC analysis revealed that PNI had the highest diagnostic accuracy for predicting early-stage malignancy (AUC: 0.757), followed by PLR (AUC: 0.700), NLR (AUC: 0.691), and CALLY (AUC: 0.690). In multivariate logistic regression models, PNI (OR: 0.870), CALLY (OR: 0.360), NLR (OR: 2.204), and PLR emerged as independent predictors of malignancy, outperforming the standard tumor marker CA 19 - 9.
CONCLUSION: Cost-effective and non-invasive immuno-nutritional indices, particularly PNI and CALLY, are promising independent predictors with high diagnostic value that may complement traditional clinical evaluation in differentiating early-stage pancreatic masses from benign lesions.

items.title: DNASE1L3 as a prognostic biomarker associated with immune cell infiltration in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is a highly aggressive malignancy, associated with a poor prognosis and a five-year survival rate of less than 9%. Although DNASE1L3 is known as an apoptosis-related gene, its specific role in cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the function of DNASE1L3 in PAAD.
METHODS: We performed an analysis of DNASE1L3 expression using the University of California Santa Cruz (UCSC) Xena platform and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases to evaluate its prognostic significance in PAAD. Co-expression analysis, Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, as well as Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), were conducted to investigate the functional pathways. Immune cell infiltration was assessed using correlation analysis. Experimental validation was carried out using lentivirus-mediated overexpression, CCK-8 assay, subcutaneous tumor xenograft models, flow cytometry for apoptosis analysis, and immunofluorescence staining.
RESULTS: DNASE1L3 expression was elevated in PAAD tissues compared with normal pancreatic tissues. Its expression showed no significant correlation with tumor stage but was positively associated with overall survival (OS) (P = 0.006). Enrichment analyzes suggested its role in immune-related pathways. GSEA highlighted upregulation in tumor immunity and migration pathways. DNASE1L3 expression was positively associated with CD8 T cells (r = 0.4, P = 0.00029), negatively correlated with macrophages (r = -0.42, P = 0.00013) and NK cells (r = -0.28, P = 0.012) in bulk deconvolution analysis, and correlated with 16 immune checkpoints. Overexpression significantly inhibited cell proliferation, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in vivo. Additionally, it enhanced anti-tumor immunity and increased oxaliplatin (Oxa) sensitivity.
CONCLUSION: The elevated expression of DNASE1L3 in PAAD is associated with a better prognosis. It correlates with immune cell infiltration, modulates the tumor immune microenvironment, and may enhance chemotherapy sensitivity. Although DNASE1L3 has been reported to be associated with poor outcomes in other malignancies, its immune-modulatory role may explain the positive prognostic association in PAAD.

items.title: Treatment of chronic pancreatitis with pancreatic duct obstruction in clinical practice: An international expert survey and case vignette study.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current international guidelines for the management of symptomatic chronic pancreatitis (CP) with pancreatic ductal obstruction differ and assign a limited role to advanced endoscopic therapies, including pancreatoscopy-guided intraductal lithotripsy. The aim of this multidisciplinary international survey is to provide an overview of current expert opinion of pancreatologists pertaining to the role of advanced endoscopic treatment in symptomatic CP with ductal obstruction.
METHODS: An international online survey was conducted among pancreatologists that were systematically selected by being affiliated to member associations for pancreatic diseases and a literature search.
RESULTS: Among the 95 pancreatologists, 59 (62%) were gastroenterologists and 36 (38%) were surgeons with a median clinical experience of 15 years (IQR 9-25). The majority (65%) did not support the most recent recommendation of the ASGE favoring primary surgery. Nearly all pancreatologists (95%) agreed that a subset of patients with CP is initially best managed endoscopically. 86% of gastroenterologists reported performing pancreatoscopy-guided intraductal lithotripsy in the management of CP. 81% of pancreatologists identified the presence of pancreatic duct stones in the head (>5 mm) with upstream ductal dilatation (>5 mm) as key finding favoring endoscopy. In contrast, surgery was favored in patients with an enlarged pancreatic head (>4 cm), stones in the pancreatic tail, or intraparenchymal calcifications by 52%, 66% and 57%.
CONCLUSION: This international expert survey demonstrates that, despite current international guideline recommendations, most pancreatologists still favor an (advanced) endoscopy first approach, rather than primary surgery in selected CP patients with ductal obstruction. Further research is warranted to better define the role of novel endoscopic therapies and to optimize patient selection for intervention.

items.title: CENPT Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Progression by Activating the RAF/MEK/ERK Signaling Pathway and Triggering MIF-Mediated Immunosuppression.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most devastating malignancies, with its incidence and mortality rates remaining particularly discouraging. Elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving PDAC progression and identifying potential therapeutic targets are critical to improve the clinical prognosis of PDAC patients. Accumulating evidence has highlighted the pivotal functions of centromere proteins (CENPs) in tumor progression. Accordingly, this study aimed to screen and identify key CENP family members implicated in PDAC pathogenesis. Through systematic analysis of CENP family proteins in PDAC, we identified CENPT as a critical regulator involved in disease progression. We further validated that CENPT promoted the proliferation and metastasis of PDAC cells via activating the RAF/MEK/ERK signaling pathway through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments. In addition, CENPT was also found to be implicated in tumor microenvironment remodeling. Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses demonstrated that CENPT expression was positively correlated with Treg cell abundance and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Further experiments suggested that CENPT upregulated the synthesis and secretion of MIF in PDAC cells, which acted on naive CD4+ T cells to promote the differentiation into Treg cells. This process ultimately induced the formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and facilitated PDAC progression, whereas blockade of MIF enhanced the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade for PDAC. In conclusion, this study revealed the crucial role of CENPT in PDAC progression, and targeting CENPT may serve as one of the potential therapeutic strategies for PDAC.

items.title: Oncolytic vaccinia virus targeting HSP70 exhibits significant cytotoxic effects on pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), known as the king of cancers, has very limited treatment options and drugs. Oncolytic viruses have been used in tumor biologic therapy, but their therapeutic efficacy is restricted due to low replication levels within tumor cells. Recently, we constructed a novel recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus (oncoVV-shHSP70) by homologous recombination of HSP70 shRNA into the TK region, which exhibited strong replication capability and cytotoxicity in PDAC. Preliminary mechanistic studies suggested that oncoVV-shHSP70 may elevate ROS levels by inhibiting activation of the NRF2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway, thereby triggering the caspase cascade and inducing apoptosis. Additionally, the virus modulated transcription levels of cytokine-related genes. In BALB/c nude mouse models, oncoVV-shHSP70 significantly suppressed tumor growth, demonstrating potent antitumor activity. In C57BL/6 immunocompetent mice, oncoVV-shHSP70 was preliminarily found to increase CD8⁺ T cell infiltration. The results of this study support the potential of oncoVV-shHSP70 as a novel strategy for PDAC, warranting further investigation.

items.title: Neuroendocrine Tumors Metastatic to the Pancreas Can Mimic Primary Pancreatic Well-Differentiated Neuroendocrine Tumors: Clinical and Pathologic Features in a Multi-Institutional and International Study.
items.abstract: Extrapancreatic well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) can metastasize to the pancreas and mimic primary pancreatic NETs (PanNETs). We analyzed 12 patients with pathologically confirmed pancreatic involvement by NET and a documented extrapancreatic primary, comparing their immunophenotype with that of 195 primary PanNETs. The primary site was assigned independently of the immunohistochemical panel under investigation, using clinical and radiologic findings, disease distribution, and comparative morphology. Direct comparison of the primary and pancreatic tumors was possible in 9 cases and demonstrated concordant morphology. Ileal NETs accounted for 9 of 12 cases (75%); the other arose in the lung (n = 2) and kidney (n = 1). All 9 ileal metastases expressed serotonin and CDX2, and 8 of 9 expressed SATB2. Compared with primary PanNETs, metastatic NETs more frequently expressed serotonin (11/12 [92%] vs. 20/195 [10%]), SATB2 (9/12 [75%] vs. 14/165 [8%]), and CDX2 (9/12 [75%] vs. 17/190 [9%]). Conversely, ISL1 (2/12 [17%] vs. 139/186 [75%]) and ARX (1/12 [8%] vs. 124/187 [66%]) were more frequently expressed in primary PanNETs (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.001). Because most metastatic tumors were of ileal origin, these associations largely reflect an ileal immunophenotype and should not be interpreted as site-independent estimates of diagnostic performance. Determining tumor origin requires clinical history, imaging, comparative morphology, and targeted immunohistochemistry. Serotonin, SATB2, and CDX2 expression may support an ileal origin, whereas expression of ISL1 and ARX may support a pancreatic origin; no individual marker is definitive.

items.title: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Progression Is Associated With Reduced Stromal Organization and Adaptive Tumor Signaling at Single-Cell Resolution.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive cancer with a poor survival rate. Publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were analyzed to characterize transcriptional changes across 33 PDAC and three normal pancreas samples. Early-stage samples exhibited greater stromal abundance and were enriched for microenvironmental remodeling, whereas advanced-stage samples showed increased proliferation and cellular plasticity. Chemotherapy-treated tumors demonstrated remodeling enrichment alongside reduced immune activity, suggesting adaptive changes. COMET analysis identified SNCG and LY6D as candidate basal-like tumor markers, supporting molecular subtype as a source of transcriptional heterogeneity. These findings highlight distinct tumor microenvironment characteristics between PDAC subtypes and progression.

items.title: Nerve proximity and high endothelial venules mark tertiary lymphoid structure niches associated with survival in advanced pancreatic cancer: an autopsy study.
items.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are generally associated with favorable outcomes in treatment-naïve pancreatic cancer, but their relevance in advanced disease remains unclear. Here, we investigated TLS prevalence and histological features in advanced pancreatic/periampullary cancer in a research autopsy cohort. Primary and metastatic tumor tissue from 19 patients was screened for TLSs using histology, duplex immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. TLSs were classified by maturation stage, high endothelial venule (HEV) presence and proximity to nerves. Associations with tissue site, chemotherapy exposure, and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Across 480 postmortem tumor blocks, 279 TLSs were identified in 38 TLS-positive blocks, predominantly from primary tumors. TLSs were more abundant and larger in primary tumors than in metastases. Only early TLSs and primary follicle-like TLSs were observed; no secondary follicle-like TLSs. TLS counts or size were not associated with OS. TLSs containing HEVs were, on average, larger than HEV-negative TLSs and tended to associate with prolonged OS, in particular in metastatic niches. Moreover, TLSs located in proximity to nerves were positively associated with OS, and the number of nerve-associated TLSs correlated with survival. Notably, the number of nerve-associated TLSs was also positively associated with the number of HEV-containing TLSs. Collectively, the findings from this exploratory study indicate that TLSs in advanced pancreatic cancer are heterogeneous and predominantly immature, with limited prognostic value based on TLS counts alone. Instead, specific microenvironmental features, particularly nerve proximity, may more accurately capture clinically relevant aspects of TLS biology in advanced disease.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE versus standard systemic therapies in advanced well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) present a therapeutic challenge due to their heterogeneity and variable response to systemic therapies. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE in patients with advanced well-differentiated GEP-NETs.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 129 patients diagnosed with advanced well-differentiated GEP-NETs between January 2022 and December 2025. Patients were classified into two groups according to treatment strategy: the [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE group (n = 65) and the control group (n = 64), who received standard systemic therapies without PRRT. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary outcomes included objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and treatment-related adverse events. Prognostic factors for OS and PFS were evaluated using Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: The median duration of follow-up was 34.6 months (1.3-45.7) in the [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE group and 25.8 months (0.9-45.6) in the control group. The [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE group demonstrated significantly longer median OS (34.6 vs. 25.8 months; P = 0.046) and median PFS (22.0 vs. 16.7 months; P = 0.008) compared with the control group. ORR showed a trend toward improvement (P = 0.118), while DCR was significantly higher in the [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE group (P = 0.026). The overall incidence of adverse events and the rates of grade ≥ 3 adverse events were comparable between groups (P > 0.05). Multivariable analysis identified [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE treatment, younger age, lower Ki-67 index, and lower tumor grade as independent predictors of improved OS or PFS.
CONCLUSION: [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE provides meaningful survival benefits with acceptable safety in patients with advanced well-differentiated GEP-NETs, supporting its integration into real-world treatment strategies and warranting further prospective validation.

items.title: HNF1A is a novel BRD4 target and critical for BET-inhibitor response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an exceedingly lethal cancer that lacks actionable molecular drivers. We previously identified the transcription factor, HNF1A, as a novel driver of tumorigenesis, stemness, and metastasis in PDAC; however, HNF1A-targeting modalities do not currently exist. Here we show that HNF1A is a direct target of BRD4, with HNF1A's expression, PDAC cell proliferation, and stemness exquisitely sensitive to BET-inhibitors (BETi), all of which can be overcome by HNF1A re-expression in a panel of PDAC cell models. RNA-sequencing analyses revealed that a subset of BETi-responsive transcripts is dependent on HNF1A expression, including multiple components of EGFR/ERBB3-signaling, with EGFR-inhibitors able to overcome HNF1A's protective effects. We found that expressions of HNF1A, BRD4, and ERBB3 were strongly correlated across PDAC patient samples, further supporting the relevancy of this regulatory axis to the disease. These findings establish HNF1A as a novel, critical target and determinant of BETi in PDAC.

items.title: PDAC BioPortal: An Integrated Web Resource for Multi-Scale Analysis of Pancreatic Cancer Transcriptomics
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits profound cellular heterogeneity and treatment-associated remodeling, yet bulk, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomic datasets remain fragmented across separate portals. We developed PDAC BioPortal, an open-access, browser-based web resource integrating four complementary human PDAC cohorts: primary tumor versus normal pancreas (TCGA-PAAD and GTEx, n = 345), a neoadjuvant stereotactic body radiotherapy-containing bulk cohort (GSE225767, n = 55), a single-nucleus chemoradiotherapy atlas (GSE202051, 224,988 nuclei across 43 patients), and 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics (GSE274103, 23,436 spots across five tumors). The platform provides interactive differential expression, rank-based pathway enrichment, patient-level pseudobulk comparisons, survival exploration, and spatial visualization, alongside PDACopilot, a deterministic, evidence-grounded natural-language query interface. Across cohorts, neoadjuvant-treated bulk and single-nucleus pathway rankings showed significant concordance, while Kitagawa-Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition and compositional sensitivity testing separated epithelial debulking from cell-intrinsic signaling shifts. Interrogation of the NRF2-associated redox network illustrated how bulk changes diverge from cell-type-resolved and spatial patterns, while continuous Cox modeling linked higher NRF2-signature expression to shorter overall survival. PDAC BioPortal is freely available at https://limboper89.github.io/PAAD-SBRT-GEx-Dashboard/. Availability: https://limboper89.github.io/PAAD-SBRT-GEx-Dashboard/

items.title: Non-invasive Prediction of Molecular and Histopathological Subtypes in Murine and Human Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Using [18F]FDG PET
items.abstract: Purpose This study evaluates the utility of [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ([ 18 F]FDG PET) for Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) subtype differentiation across preclinical and clinical settings, and assesses the impact of tracer uptake timing on subtype discrimination. Methods [ 18 F]FDG uptake was investigated in classical (C)-HPAC and quasi-mesenchymal (QM)-PSN1 cells, heterotopic rat (n = 11), orthotopic mouse xenografts (n = 8), and gland-forming (GF)/non-GF tumors from seven genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs). Retrospective [ 18 F]FDG PET data from 16 PDAC patients were analyzed using subtype classification based on keratin-81 (KRT81+(QM)/KRT81-(non-QM)). Dynamic and static [ 18 F]FDG PET parameters, including standard uptake value (SUV) mean , SUV max , and mean tumor-to-muscle ratio (T/M mean ), were evaluated for subtype discrimination. Results QM tumors showed significantly higher [ 18 F]FDG uptake than C tumors in vitro (50.7 ± 1.03% vs. 19.4 ± 2.37%), in heterotopic (SUV max 6.91 ± 1.14 vs. 2.66 ± 0.28), and orthotopic (SUV max 2.85 ± 0.70 vs. 1.45 ± 0.50) xenografts. Non-GF tumors also showed significantly higher uptake than GF (SUV max 3.94 ± 0.70 vs. 2.53 ± 0.97). Patients showed a similar trend (SUV max 6.33 ± 1.74 vs. 4.95 ± 1.46), with shorter overall survival in QM tumors. Dynamic PET revealed continued tracer accumulation in QM/non-GF tumors throughout the 90-minute acquisition period, whereas C/GF tumors approached a plateau by approximately 60 minutes. T/M mean showed the best classification performance across all models. Conclusion [ 18 F]FDG PET differentiated PDAC subtypes across all preclinical models with a similar but less pronounced trend in patients. Later imaging time points showed enhanced metabolic separation, suggesting potential benefits for improving non-invasive subtype discrimination. Clinical Trial Registration N/A

items.title: Diagnostic performance and interobserver agreement of MRI for pancreatic cystic lesions: a multi-reader study with surgical histopathologic correlation.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the diagnostic performance and interobserver agreement of MRI for differentiating mucinous from non-mucinous pancreatic cystic lesions (PCLs) and identifying advanced neoplasia using surgical pathology as the reference standard.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included surgically resected PCLs with preoperative MRI (2019-2025). Three independent readers blindly assessed cyst subtype and imaging features, including worrisome features (WF) and high-risk stigmata (HRS) according to the 2024 Kyoto guideline. Consensus interpretation was established with a fourth senior abdominal radiologist. Diagnostic performance for mucinous lesion characterization and advanced neoplasia (high-grade dysplasia and invasive carcinoma) was evaluated. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Fleiss κ and Gwet AC1. Logistic regression and ROC analyses identified imaging predictors of advanced neoplasia.
RESULTS: A total of 85 patients were included (mean age, 66.8 ± 12.5 years; 50.6 % female). At pathology, 70/85 lesions (82.4 %) were mucinous and 23/85 (27.1 %) represented advanced neoplasia, including 21 high-grade dysplasia and two IPMN-derived PDAC. MRI consensus interpretation achieved 100 % sensitivity, 80 % specificity, and 96.5 % accuracy for identifying mucinous lesions. MRI demonstrated 52.2 % sensitivity and 67.7 % specificity for advanced neoplasia using WF or HRS, whereas HRS alone improved specificity (95.2 %) at the expense of sensitivity (21.7 %). All readers correctly identified both cases of IPMN-derived PDAC. Interobserver agreement for cyst subtype classification was fair by Fleiss κ but substantial by Gwet AC1, whereas agreement for detecting advanced neoplasia was moderate. Main pancreatic duct diameter independently predicted advanced neoplasia (OR, 1.18; 95 % CI, 1.01-1.38; p = 0.042) and outperformed cyst size (AUC, 0.69 vs 0.56).
CONCLUSION: In this surgically selected cohort, consensus MRI differentiates mucinous from nonmucinous PCLs with high sensitivity. Detection of advanced neoplasia, particularly noninvasive high-grade dysplasia, remains challenging because of overlap with low-grade lesions. Fair-to-moderate interobserver agreement highlights the challenges of MRI-based risk stratification. The surgically selected cohort provides histopathologic confirmation but should be considered when interpreting performance estimates in the broader surveillance population.

items.title: ATAT1-dependent microtubule acetylation drives pancreatic tumorigenesis through DNMT1-mediated regulation of NDRG4.
items.abstract: Microtubule (MT) acetylation is frequently elevated in cancer and associated with poor prognosis. Alpha-tubulin acetyltransferase 1 (ATAT1), the principal enzyme responsible for this modification, has therefore emerged as a potential therapeutic target. However, which cancer types depend on ATAT1 activity and are selectively vulnerable to its inhibition remains unclear. Here, using a phospho-specific marker of ATAT1 activity, we identify pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) as an ATAT1-dependent malignancy. ATAT1 activity is elevated in human PDAC and genetically engineered mouse models, emerging during pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia and persisting in a substantial subset of tumors. Genetic inactivation or pharmacologic inhibition of ATAT1 suppresses PDAC cell growth, reduces orthotopic tumor burden, and markedly inhibits tumor initiation in KPC mice without overt toxicity. Mechanistically, ATAT1-dependent MT acetylation sustains Akt signaling, resulting in inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β and stabilization of the DNA methyltransferase DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1). Elevated DNMT1 promotes repression of tumor suppressor genes, including NDRG4, whereas inhibition of ATAT1 or DNMT1 restores NDRG4 expression and impairs tumor growth. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized ATAT1-Akt-GSK3β-DNMT1 signaling axis linking cytoskeletal acetylation to NDRG4 repression and reveal ATAT1 as a therapeutic vulnerability during the early stages of pancreatic tumorigenesis.

items.title: Oligometastatic and Oligoprogressive Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: New Frontiers for Local Therapy.
items.abstract: Oligometastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) represents a distinct clinical state in which carefully selected patients may benefit from local consolidative therapy (LCT) in addition to systemic therapy. Standardized consensus definitions, retrospective studies, and the randomized phase II EXTEND trial have established the foundation for prospective evaluation of LCT in this population. In this review, we summarize evolving definitions of oligometastatic and oligoprogressive PDAC, review current evidence supporting LCT, and highlight ongoing prospective studies designed to validate its role and refine patient selection. We also discuss emerging opportunities to integrate biomarkers into future treatment paradigms. Collectively, these advances are shifting the field toward biology-informed, multidisciplinary management of patients with oligometastatic and oligoprogressive PDAC.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Management of Patients With Nonmetastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains among the most lethal malignancies; however, outcomes for patients with nonmetastatic disease have improved substantially over the past decade. Historically, management centered on upfront surgical resection, but treatment paradigms have evolved toward multidisciplinary strategies incorporating neoadjuvant systemic therapy, selective use of radiation, perioperative optimization, and individualized surgical approaches. Increased emphasis is placed on tumor biology, treatment response, and patient condition in addition to traditional anatomic definitions of resectability. Advances in systemic therapies, molecular profiling, prehabilitation, and perioperative care have expanded treatment opportunities and improved outcomes. This review summarizes contemporary multidisciplinary management of nonmetastatic PDAC, ongoing controversies, and future directions.

items.title: The Emerging Role for Precision Medicine in Pancreatic Cancer.
items.abstract: Systemic therapy has now evolved as the initial treatment for all stages of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Although conventional cytotoxic chemotherapy remains the backbone of PDAC management, the selection of specific regimens is still largely empiric. The emergence of effective biomarker-directed therapies, including RAS inhibitors, PRMT5 inhibitors, and PARP inhibitors, has ushered in a new era of individualized, precision oncology approaches for patients with PDAC. Realizing the full potential of these therapeutic advances, however, requires parallel progress in the tools available to clinicians for their application. In this review, we examine recent advances in functional precision oncology in PDAC, with particular emphasis on preclinical models, molecular tumor boards, and innovative clinical trial designs. We also share insights from the experience of the LaBahn Pancreatic Program at the Medical College of Wisconsin in addressing the practical challenges of implementing precision oncology for patients with PDAC.

items.title: Targeting RAS Signaling Pathways: Molecular Regulation, FDA-Approved Inhibitors, Clinical Advances, and Patent Innovations.
items.abstract: RAS gene mutations play a major role in the development and progression of cancer. According to recent data, mutations in the RAS gene are responsible for nearly 30% of all cancer cases worldwide. Among these, KRAS mutations account for more than 85% of all RAS mutations and are particularly prevalent in aggressive malignancies, including colorectal cancer (CRC), non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). In this manuscript, we provide a detailed discussion of the RAS signaling cascades and their regulatory mechanisms. The catalytic region of RAS proteins, which comprises the P-loop, Switch I and Switch II regions, and RAS-effector interaction surfaces, exhibits a high degree of structural conservation across the different RAS isoforms. Sotorasib was the first covalent KRAS inhibitor to receive regulatory approval and acts by irreversibly binding to the cysteine residue at position 12 (Cys12). In this manuscript, we discuss in detail targeted RAS inhibitors, including adagrasib (MRTX849), fulzerasib (IBI351), garsorasib (D-1553), glecirasib (JAB-21822), and divarasib (GDC-6036). Finally, we focus on recent advances in RAS inhibitor patents from 2019 to the present, with particular emphasis on thiazole, benzothiazole, quinazoline, and other emerging chemical scaffolds.

items.title: SMAD4 Protein Expression and Survival Outcomes in Resected PDAC
items.abstract:
Background:

/Objectives: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited prognostic biomarkers after curative-intent resection. We aim to determine if loss of SMAD4 protein expression has prognostic significance in operated PDAC patients.

Methods:

SMAD4 protein expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in resected PDAC tu-mours from patients treated at two centers. The prognostic significance of SMAD4 expression status and clinical outcomes, namely overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS), was assessed using survival analysis with Kaplan–Meier estimation and Cox proportional hazards regression models.

Results:

A total of 87 patients with resected PDAC were included in the final analysis, with a median follow-up of 75.9 months. In univariable analysis, SMAD4 expression status was not associated with OS (intact vs. lost: HR = 0.87, p = 0.56) or RFS (HR = 0.84, p = 0.51). In multivariable analysis, SMAD4 expression was not an independent prognostic factor for OS (HR = 0.94, p = 0.81) or RFS (HR = 0.82, p = 0.49). Established clinicopathological variables, including histological grade, nodal status, postoperative CA19-9 levels, and adju-vant treatment, were independently associated with both survival outcomes, while resection status was inde-pendently associated with OS.

Conclusions:

In this bicentric cohort, loss of SMAD4 expression assessed by IHC was not an independent prognostic marker for OS or RFS of resected PDAC. Despite the potential SMAD4 relevance within specific biological or clinical subgroups, further studies are warranted to clarify the role of SMAD4 in PDAC risk strati-fication and support the development of integrated molecular and clinicopathological prognostic models.

items.title: Targeting SUMOylation in Combination with Agonistic Anti-CD40 Therapy Activates Anti- Tumor Immunity to Control Pancreatic Cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains an aggressive, lethal form of cancer and available immunotherapies are ineffective for most patients. In this study, we investigated combining agonistic anti-CD40 (aCD40) with TAK-981 (TAK/subasumstat), a SUMOylation inhibitor with immune priming effects. We previously reported that TAK-981 increases CD40 expression on antigen-presenting cells, and thus we hypothesized that combining it with an agonistic CD40 antibody (aCD40) would enhance immune-mediated tumor control. We investigated the therapeutic effect of TAK-981 + aCD40 in vivo using three syngeneic, orthotopic mouse models of PDAC. Single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence/immunohistochemistry were used to identify immunogenic changes in the tumor microenvironment. T-cell and macrophage depletions were used to assess functional contributions of individual immune cell populations. We assessed the functional contributions of T-cells and macrophages by depleting their populations separately.TAK-981+aCD40 treatment augmented CD8+ T-cell and macrophage infiltration into the tumor, amplified IFNα and IFNγ signaling, decreased TGFβ signaling and increased MHC-I expression resulting in decreased tumor burden and improved median survival. Despite the induction of dramatic CD8+ T cell infiltration into tumors, the efficacy of combination therapy was not impacted by T cell deficiency or depletion. In contrast, depletion of phagocytic macrophages abolished the therapeutic benefit of combination therapy. Therefore, TAK-981+aCD40 combination therapy activates macrophage mediated anti-tumor immunity in the PDAC models. Our findings support further exploration of this combination in clinical trials to validate this combination as a strategy to generate meaningful macrophage-mediated anti-tumor immune responses in pancreatic cancer patients.

items.title: A biomimetic desmoplastic pancreatic cancer organoid model reveals macrophage contributions to stiffness-associated chemoresistance.
items.abstract: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the tumor microenvironment (TME) is characterized by a desmoplastic stroma that is markedly stiffer than normal pancreatic tissue. While increased extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness has been shown to promote chemoresistance in tumor cells, the impact of these biophysical cues on tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) has yet to be fully explored. This gap is due in part to the lack of model systems that recapitulate both stiff environments and macrophage involvement. To address this limitation, we developed a biomimetic, three-dimensional (3D) co-culture model that integrates PDAC organoids, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), and macrophages within tunable fibrotic matrices that recapitulate the stiff ECM of the PDAC microenvironment. Using this 3D system, we demonstrate that CAF-mediated matrix remodeling drives increased stiffness and enhances chemoresistance of PDAC organoids, effects not captured in conventional two-dimensional stiffness platforms. Incorporation of macrophages into the model further amplified this protective effect, with stiff tri-culture conditions exhibiting minimal response to gemcitabine compared to organoid-CAF cultures alone. In this context, matrix stiffness and tumor-derived cues altered macrophage behavior, including reduced M1-associated marker expression. Application of the model further identified TRPV4 signaling as a contributor to stiffness-associated chemoresistance, as pharmacological inhibition of TRPV4 sensitized organoids to gemcitabine treatment within stiff tri-cultures. Together, these findings establish a biomimetic platform for investigating immune-stromal-tumor interactions within the mechanically complex PDAC microenvironment and demonstrate how CAF-driven matrix remodeling can reveal biologically relevant mechanisms of therapeutic resistance that are not apparent in simplified model systems.

items.title: Integrating metabolism and immunity: targeting lactate-mediated mechanisms in PDAC.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a poor prognosis and responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Lactate is abundant in the tumor microenvironment and is associated with immune evasion. This study examined the regulatory role of lactate and evaluated metabolism-immunity targeting strategies in PDAC.
METHODS: We used PDAC cell models exposed to lactate and xenograft mice, applying N1-methyladenosine RNA immunoprecipitation, ribosome profiling, and transcriptome analyses to examine lactate's effects via the TRMT6-SIRT5 axis. The efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitors combined with lactate metabolism blockers was also tested.
RESULTS: Lactate significantly enhanced N1-methyladenosine RNA modification by TRMT6, increasing translation of key metabolic enzymes and driving reprogramming. It activated SIRT5-mediated desuccinylation, boosting TCA cycle enzyme activity and oxidative metabolism. Lactate upregulated PD-L1 via the TRMT6-SIRT5 axis, enhancing CDK4/6 signaling and immune evasion. Combining lactate blockers with CDK4/6 inhibitors reduced PD-L1 expression, restored T cell function, and improved anti-PD-1 therapy efficacy in mice.
CONCLUSIONS: Lactate may promote metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion in PDAC through the TRMT6-SIRT5 axis, linking metabolism, epigenetic regulation, and antitumor immunity. Combining CDK4/6 inhibition with lactate blockade may provide a rationale for improving immunotherapy responses in pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outlines current computational and experimental techniques to identify, prioritise, and functionally validate non-coding variants in PDAC. We discuss in silico methods including genome-wide association study (GWAS) fine-mapping, colocalisation, machine learning-driven functional annotation, and the use of established computational tools, in addition to epigenomic profiling technologies including, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, and CUT&RUN which define regulatory landscapes. We also emphasise new AI-based methods involving radiogenomics, AI imaging analysis and data integration, which provides novel potential to link genomic variation with phenotypic and imaging characteristics. Additionally, we highlight experimental validation techniques including reporter assays, electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSA), chromatin conformation capture methods, and CRISPR-based perturbation systems used to study variant functionality. Together, these complementary approaches establish a framework for correlating non-coding variation to regulatory mechanisms in PDAC.

items.title: OSBPL3 promotes pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression through lipid metabolism reprogramming and is targeted by lupenone.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As a highly malignant neoplasm with dismal prognosis, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is closely linked to disordered lipid metabolism, which serves a key part in facilitating its pathological progression. Identifying key lipid metabolism-related genes as therapeutic targets is urgent.
METHODS: Differentially expressed genes in PDAC were screened using GEO datasets and overlapped with lipid metabolism-related genes via Venn diagram. OSBPL3 was identified as a crucial regulator in the PDAC development through expression and survival analysis. In vitro (CCK-8, Transwell, BODIPY staining, Fillipin III staining) and in vivo (xenograft models) experiments assessed its functions on PDAC progression and lipid metabolism. Molecular docking identified Lupenone as an OSBPL3 inhibitor, with validation of its effects on cell proliferation and lipid metabolism.
RESULTS: OSBPL3 was remarkably upregulated in PDAC tissues and cell lines (PANC-1, BxPC-3), correlating with poor survival. Knockdown of OSBPL3 attenuated cell viability, migration, and tumor growth, accelerated apoptosis, and suppressed lipid accumulation (lipid droplets, cholesterol, triglycerides), reduced the expression of SREBP1, ACLY, and ACC1. Lupenone targeted OSBPL3, reversed its pro-tumor effects, and reduced lipid metabolism.
CONCLUSION: OSBPL3 drives PDAC progression via lipid metabolism regulation, and Lupenone is a potential therapeutic agent targeting OSBPL3.

items.title: miR-221 and miR-222 in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: mechanistic evidence, extracellular vesicle communication, biomarker candidates, and therapeutic prospects.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to diagnose early and treat effectively. The related microRNAs miR-221 and miR-222 share a seed sequence, but their functions and clinical evidence should be evaluated individually. Pancreatic cancer models support miR-221/222-associated TIMP-2 repression and invasion, miR-222-mediated p57 regulation, and tumor-derived vesicular miR-222 effects on p27 expression and localization. Macrophage-derived extracellular vesicular miR-222-3p has also been implicated in gemcitabine resistance through TSC1-associated signaling. By contrast, the TRPS1-ZEB2 mechanism and the vesicular SPINT1-HGF liver pathway derive from breast and colorectal cancer studies, respectively, and remain extrapolations when discussed in PDAC. Circulating miR-221 has shown exploratory diagnostic associations, but results from general miRNA panels cannot be assigned to miR-221 or miR-222 individually. Tissue prognostic associations likewise do not validate circulating assays. A first-in-human study of the selective inhibitor LNA-i-miR-221 provides early safety and peripheral-blood pharmacodynamic evidence in a mixed advanced-cancer population that included pancreatic cancer; it does not establish PDAC-specific efficacy. Translation requires independent biomarker validation, molecule-specific target-dependence studies, and confirmation of effective pancreatic tumor delivery.

items.title: Inkjet-printed single cell-derived pancreatic cancer organoid for intratumoral heterogeneity quantification.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits extensive intratumoral heterogeneity that contributes to therapeutic resistance and disease recurrence. However, conventional bulk analyses often obscure the molecular and functional diversity of individual tumor cell populations, limiting the identification of rare drug-resistant populations. Here, we present a high-resolution, drop-on-demand inkjet bioprinting platform for generating single cell-derived PDAC organoids to systematically investigate clonal heterogeneity. Using this platform, we generated over 600 organoids and characterized substantial variations in morphology, growth kinetics, protein expression, and chemotherapeutic responses. Transcriptomic profiling of 30 individual organoids further revealed pronounced molecular heterogeneity, even among organoids assigned to the same morphological subtype. Notably, morphology-based classification into classical and basal-like subtypes did not consistently correspond to transcriptomic signatures, demonstrating that morphological similarity does not necessarily reflect molecular similarity. Furthermore, individual organoids exhibited heterogeneous responses to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, including highly resistant organoids whose responses were obscured by subtype-averaged analyses. Together, these findings establish an inkjet-based clonal organoid platform that integrates controlled single-cell deposition with molecular profiling and longitudinal drug-response analysis, enabling systematic characterization of morphological, molecular, and functional heterogeneity at the individual organoid level.

items.title: Outcomes of Pancreatectomy with Superior Mesenteric Artery Resection: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior mesenteric artery (SMA) involvement is commonly considered a contraindication to surgical resection in locally advanced pancreatic cancer. The role of SMA resection during pancreatectomy remains controversial, with historical data suggesting prohibitive morbidity and poor survival.
METHODS: A systematic search of the literature was performed. Studies reporting on patients undergoing pancreatectomy with concomitant SMA resection were included. Primary endpoints were perioperative morbidity, 90-day mortality, and survival. Additional data on neoadjuvant treatment, patient selection, anticoagulation, reconstruction techniques, and oncological outcomes were also extracted.
RESULTS: In total, 12 studies reporting on 320 patients undergoing pancreatectomy with SMA resection were included. All included studies showed a serious risk of bias and described highly selected patients. Concomitant venous resection was performed in 97% (n = 244/252) of patients and a total pancreatectomy in 63% (n = 173/275). Arterial reconstruction was achieved by graft interposition in 48% (n = 128/269), primary end-to-end anastomosis in 39% (n = 106/269), and splenic artery transposition in 13% (n = 34/269) of patients. Major morbidity and 90-day mortality were 31% (n = 88/284) and 8% (n = 27/320), respectively. Complications included post-pancreatectomy hemorrhage in 19% (n = 39/202) of patients and mesenteric ischemia in 3% (n = 6/202). R0 resection was achieved in 80% (n = 136/171) of patients. Median reported survival from surgery ranged from 8 to 20 months. The highest reported 5-year survival was 21%.
CONCLUSIONS: Pancreatectomy with SMA resection is associated with specific perioperative morbidity and an 8% mortality rate. Since these outcomes were achieved by expert groups under highly selected circumstances, only implementation at high-volume centers with dedicated vascular pancreatic surgery expertise should be considered.

items.title: An asymmetric split-costimulatory MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 dual CAR-T design enhances activity against antigenically heterogeneous pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a highly lethal solid tumor with limited responsiveness to chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy. A major challenge is antigen heterogeneity, which allows antigen-low or antigen-negative tumor cells to escape immune pressure. Here, we identified mesothelin (MSLN) and NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs) as a complementary antigen pair in PDAC, showing frequent but discordant expression in clinical specimens. Based on this, we generated single-target, tandem, and dual CAR constructs against MSLN and/or NKG2DLs and compared their antitumor activity. Among them, an asymmetric split-costimulatory dual-CAR, MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28, showed the best overall performance. MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 CAR-T cells efficiently eliminated single-positive, double-positive, and mixed-antigen tumor populations, sustained serial killing, produced higher effector cytokines, and preserved a less exhausted, more memory-like phenotype in vitro. In vivo, MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 CAR-T achieved stronger tumor control, greater intratumoral accumulation, improved persistence, and prolonged survival in pancreatic tumor models, including those mimicking antigen heterogeneity. Transcriptomic, biochemical, and pharmacologic analyses further identified IL-2-STAT5 signaling as an important pathway supporting the enhanced fitness and antitumor activity of this construct. Together, these findings show that dual targeting alone is insufficient; the arrangement of receptor inputs and costimulatory signals strongly influences therapeutic output. This study identifies MSLN.BBz/NKG2D.28 as a promising dual-CAR strategy for PDAC.

items.title: High-Sensitivity Detection of Early Pancreatic Cancer Using a Structured Scoring System Among Clinically Selected Outpatients: A Nationwide Prospective Study.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the diagnostic performance of a structured scoring system integrating multiple pancreatic cancer (PC)-relevant factors for detecting early-stage PC among clinically selected outpatients.
METHODS: In this nationwide multicenter prospective cohort study, consecutive physician-selected outpatients undergoing initial endoscopic ultrasonography for mild symptoms, risk factors, or subtle imaging abnormalities were enrolled. Risk factors were categorized as low- or high-grade relevance (LGR/HGR), with one point per factor. A positive score was defined as LGR ≥ 3 and/or HGR ≥ 1. Diagnostic performance for high-grade dysplasia (HGD)/stage 1 PC was compared with that of conventional symptom-, family history-, and genetic risk-based approaches within this cohort.
RESULTS: Among 3269 patients, 2525 were score-positive and 744 were score-negative. For HGD/stage 1 PC, the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 93.2%, 23.1%, 2.7%, and 99.3%, respectively. Sensitivity significantly exceeded that of conventional approaches (93.2% vs. 56.8%, p < 0.001), although paired comparison using the conditional relative odds ratio (CROR) showed no significant difference (CROR, 1.79; 95% CI, 0.54-5.90; p = 0.34). HGD/stage 1 PC detection was significantly higher in score-positive than in score-negative patients (2.7% vs. 0.7%, p = 0.001). Among PCs detected in score-positive patients, 24.3% were HGD/stage 1.
CONCLUSIONS: The scoring system demonstrated high cross-sectional sensitivity for HGD/stage 1 PC detection among clinically selected outpatients undergoing detailed PC evaluation. Its utility for selecting patients from unselected general outpatient populations remains unestablished. Prospective validation in consecutive general outpatients with systematic longitudinal follow-up is warranted.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the University Hospital Medical Network Clinical Trials Registry (http://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm) as UMIN000034832 on December 1, 2018.

items.title: Unifying functional experimental systems with clinical predictive technologies for personalized care in PDAC.
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a clinical challenge, projected to become the second leading cause of cancer-related death by 2030. Traditional research has historically relied on established PDAC-derived cell lines to establish 2D in vitro models or in vivo xenografts for drug discovery. These approaches, however, fail to encompass the complexity of PDAC and few studies have been translated into game-changing treatments for patients with pancreatic cancer. This review advocates for a paradigm shift through the integration of complementary modeling strategies. We provide a comprehensive evaluation of more sophisticated in vitro systems, such as 3D models (spheroids and organoids), co-cultures and microfluidics, which offer scalable platforms for high-throughput screening and mechanistic analysis. Likewise, we emphasize the indispensable role of in vivo models, including genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs) for studying stepwise progression and immune evasion, and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) for capturing human-specific drug sensitivities and intratumoral heterogeneity. Beyond functional models, we explore the clinical utility of transcriptomic profiling to define PDAC subtypes, facilitating real-time patient stratification in landmark clinical trials. We further examine the role of liquid biopsy as a dynamic tool for monitoring minimal residual disease and the emergence of treatment resistance. Finally, we discuss the future of pharmacogenomics, the "tri-genomic" influence of the microbiome, and the integration of multi-omics through artificial intelligence to optimize individual therapeutic outcomes. By unifying these diverse predictive paradigms, we aim to bridge the gap between preclinical discovery and precision oncology, fostering more effective and individualized treatment strategies for all PDAC patients.

items.title: ACSL5 suppresses pancreatic cancer progression and gemcitabine resistance by regulating n-6 docosapentaenoic acid metabolism.
items.abstract: Gemcitabine (GEM) resistance remains a major challenge in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of tumors, and imbalance in lipid metabolism promotes tumor progression and drug resistance. This study aims to elucidate the mechanism of Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long Chain Family Member 5 (ACSL5) in PDAC, its impact on fatty acid metabolism, and its clinical relevance. Through RNA sequencing, targeted metabolomics, proteomics, retrospective cohort studies, and a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, the significance of ACSL5 was systematically investigated. Our results showed that ACSL5 was downregulated in GEM-resistant cells, and its high expression predicted better survival in PDAC patients. ACSL5 overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and GEM resistance in PDAC cells, while its knockdown promoted these phenotypes. ACSL5 may exert its effects through the PPARδ/CPT1A signaling pathway, thereby influencing fatty acid β-oxidation. Notably, ACSL5 selectively modulated n-6 docosapentaenoic acid (DPA-n6) levels, while prospective cohort studies have shown that high plasma DPA-n6 is an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. Junction Plakoglobin (JUP) was identified as an ACSL5-binding protein and was associated with ACSL5 ubiquitination and protein stability. In summary, ACSL5 acts as a tumor suppressor in PDAC by modulating fatty acid metabolism. DPA-n6 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker, highlighting the clinical relevance of ACSL5-associated lipid metabolism in PDAC.

items.title: Phase I dose-escalation study of stereotactic body radiotherapy with elective nodal irradiation for borderline resectable and unresectable locally advanced pancreatic cancer.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Locoregional recurrence remains a major clinical challenge in borderline resectable (BR) and unresectable locally advanced (UR-LA) pancreatic cancer, even after stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This phase I trial evaluated the safety, maximum tolerated dose (MTD), and preliminary efficacy of adding prophylactic elective nodal irradiation (ENI) to 5-fraction SBRT.
METHODS: Patients with BR/UR-LAPC were enrolled in a 3 + 3 dose-escalation design. SBRT was delivered in 5 fractions using either adaptive magnetic resonance image-guided radiation therapy or respiratory breath-hold radiotherapy with a fiducial marker. The ENI dose was fixed at 30 Gy in five fractions, while the primary tumor dose increased from Level 1 (35 Gy) to Level 3 (40 Gy). The primary endpoint was acute dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) (any Grade ≥ 3 non-hematological adverse events within 14 days after the completion of SBRT).
RESULTS: Twelve patients (BR: 4, LA: 8) were enrolled, 11 of whom had previously received systemic chemotherapy. One patient at Level 1 experienced acute Grade 3 anorexia/nausea requiring hospitalization. No DLTs were observed at Levels 2 and 3, and the MTD was not reached. Three patients with preexisting biliary stents developed subacute Grade 3 cholangitis. No Grade ≥ 3 late adverse events occurred. The median overall survival after SBRT was 17.3 months, and the 1-year locoregional control rate was 75%.
CONCLUSION: Five-fraction SBRT with simultaneous 30 Gy ENI was feasible, and the MTD was not reached within the tested dose levels up to 40 Gy. Further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its long-term safety and treatment outcomes.
